parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Express the general point of $l$ in component form, e.g. $(1+\lambda,3-2\lambda,-2+3\lambda)$ [B1]. Substitute in the equation of $p$ and solve for $\lambda$ [M1]. Obtain $\frac53\mathbf i+\frac53\mathbf j$ from $\lambda=2/3$ [A1]. Guidance: OE; accept $1.67\mathbf i+1.67\mathbf j$ or better. Total: 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use a correct method to evaluate a scalar product of relevant vectors, e.g. $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)\mathbin{\cdot}(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$ [M1]. Using the correct process for calculating the moduli, divide the scalar product by the product of the moduli and evaluate the inverse sine or cosine of the result [M1]. Guidance: $|\sin\theta|=9/14$. Obtain $40.0^\circ$ or $0.698$ radians [A1]. Guidance: AWRT. Alternative: use a correct method to evaluate a vector product of relevant vectors, e.g. $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)\times(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$ [M1]. Using the correct process for the modulus, divide the modulus of the vector product by the product of the moduli and evaluate the inverse sine or cosine [M1]. Guidance: $\cos\theta=\sqrt{115}/14$. Obtain $40.0^\circ$ or $0.698$ radians [A1], AWRT. Total: 3.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.answer: $3x+9y+5z=20$. Printed official anomaly: the third alternative on MS page 20 instead states $3x+9y+5z=2$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State $a-2b+3c=0$ or $2a+b-3c=0$ [B1]. Obtain two relevant equations and solve for one ratio, e.g. $a:b$ [M1]. Guidance: could use $2a+b-3c=0$ and $a+3b-2c=d$, $(5/3)a+(5/3)b=d$, i.e. use two points on the line rather than its direction; the second M1 is not scored until they solve for $d$. Obtain $a:b:c=3:9:5$ [A1], OE. Substitute $a,b,c$ and a relevant point in the plane equation and evaluate $d$ [M1], using their calculated normal and a relevant point. Obtain $3x+9y+5z=20$ [A1], OE. Alternative: attempt the vector product of relevant vectors, e.g. $(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)\times(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$ [M1]. Obtain two correct components [A1]. Obtain a correct answer, e.g. $3\mathbf i+9\mathbf j+5\mathbf k$ [A1]. Use the product and a relevant point to find $d$ [M1]. Obtain $3x+9y+5z=20$, or equivalent [A1], OE. Third printed alternative: attempt to form a 2-parameter equation with relevant vectors [M1]. State a correct equation, e.g. $\mathbf r=\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-2\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+3\mathbf k)+\mu(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j-3\mathbf k)$ [A1]. State 3 equations in $x,y,z,\lambda,\mu$ [A1]. Eliminate $\lambda$ and $\mu$ [M1]. The official page then prints 'Obtain answer $3x+9y+5z=2$' [A1], OE. Printed anomaly: this conflicts with the two earlier official methods on page 19 and with substitution of a point on $l$, both of which give right-hand side 20. Total: 5.
